product_family: Apache Superset: open-source data visualization and exploration platform (self-hosted); related managed offering Preset is a separate commercial entity

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 2
certifications.proof_quote: Apache Superset is open-source self-hosted software maintained by a nonprofit foundation. No managed SaaS exists under the ASF umbrella; SOC 2 audits are not applicable to OSS projects. No public evidence found on superset.apache.org or apache.org.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: ASF uses AWS (DNS) and Azure (servers) which hold ISO 27001 - those are host-level certs, not ASF/Superset certs. No evidence the Apache Software Foundation itself holds ISO 27001 certification.

certifications.name: GDPR (compliance posture)
certifications.proof_quote: ASF's own websites follow a GDPR-aligned privacy policy referencing GDPR Articles 15-21. However, Apache Superset as self-hosted software carries no GDPR certification; the deploying organization bears full GDPR responsibility for data in their Superset instance.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on superset.apache.org or apache.org. Not applicable to open-source self-hosted software; operators must configure their own HIPAA-compliant deployment.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on superset.apache.org or apache.org. PCI DSS responsibility lies with the deploying organization, not the OSS project.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not applicable to open-source self-hosted software.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI Governance)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Apache Superset does not include AI model training features; no AI governance certification found.

privacy.ai_training_note: Not applicable. Apache Superset is self-hosted software; all data stays within the deploying organization's own infrastructure. No data is transmitted to the Apache Software Foundation. The software has no built-in AI model that trains on customer query or dashboard data.
privacy.data_region: Fully operator-determined; ASF has no data residency obligations since it does not host end-user Superset instances.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: TLS 1.2+ required for production; operators must configure a reverse proxy (Nginx, Traefik, or load balancer). Superset documentation explicitly states running without HTTPS is insecure.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: SUPERSET_SECRET_KEY encrypts session cookies and metadata DB credentials (database connection strings). Application data encryption at rest is the operator's responsibility at the database and storage layer.

security.name: Authentication
security.value: Flask AppBuilder (FAB) handles auth; supports built-in DB auth, OAuth, LDAP, and SAML/SSO integration with Azure AD, Google, Okta. API key authentication available for service accounts.

security.name: Authorization / RBAC
security.value: Five built-in roles: Admin (full control), Alpha (all data sources), Gamma (assigned data sources only), sql_lab, Public. Dashboard-level RBAC via DASHBOARD_RBAC feature flag. Row Level Security (RLS) via SQL WHERE clauses with Jinja templating.

security.name: Session security
security.value: Server-side sessions recommended for production (Redis/Memcached). Cookie flags: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True, SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Lax'. Configurable session lifetime.

security.name: Content Security Policy
security.value: Via Talisman extension. Disabled by default; operators must explicitly enable for security headers. Nonce-based script execution supported.

security.name: Vulnerability disclosure
security.value: Reports to security@superset.apache.org (private). ASF acts as a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA). CVE list published at superset.apache.org/docs/security/cves.

security.name: Secrets management
security.value: SUPERSET_SECRET_KEY, GUEST_TOKEN_JWT_SECRET, GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES_JWT_SECRET must be stored in environment variables or secrets managers, never hardcoded. Quarterly rotation recommended.

products.name: Apache Superset (open-source)
products.data_scope: Connects to operator-managed databases; metadata stored in operator-managed metadata DB. No data sent to ASF.
products.notes: Self-hosted only. Apache License 2.0. Free with no per-user licensing cost. Deploying organization is solely responsible for all compliance certifications.

products.name: Preset (managed cloud, separate vendor)
products.data_scope: Multi-tenant SaaS on AWS; workspace-isolated query caching; database credentials encrypted at rest with AES-256.
products.notes: Preset Inc. is a separate commercial company, not the Apache Software Foundation. Preset holds SOC 2 Type 2, PCI-DSS Level 2, and HIPAA compliance; these certifications belong to Preset Inc., not to Apache Superset or ASF.

compare.pricing_model: Free and open-source (Apache License 2.0); infrastructure costs borne by operator
compare.data_residency: Fully operator-controlled; no ASF involvement in deployed instance data

flags: Not to be confused with trust.superset.sh, which is operated by Superset (superset.sh), a separate AI coding-agent IDE company unrelated to the Apache Superset data platform.
ASF uses AWS (ISO 27001, PCI DSS Level 1) and Azure for infrastructure. These are the cloud providers' certifications, not ASF's or Apache Superset's.

Preset Inc. (preset.io) holds SOC 2 Type 2, PCI-DSS Level 2, and HIPAA. Preset is a separate commercial company offering managed Apache Superset, and these certifications do not apply to the open-source Apache Superset project.
Standard SaaS compliance certifications such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA are not applicable to self-hosted open-source software; their absence is not a signal about software quality.
Talisman (Content Security Policy) is disabled by default; operators must explicitly enable it. HTTPS is not enforced at the application layer and requires an operator-configured reverse proxy.
The ASF does not offer a Data Processing Agreement for Superset deployers. Organizations with GDPR or data-processor requirements must manage this at their infrastructure layer.
The G-Cloud listing (629273458006122) is from Millersoft Limited, a third-party UK reseller. Its Cyber Essentials certification belongs to Millersoft, not to ASF or Apache Superset.
